text:
ben: hitting a weird latency spike on canary this morning — p50/ p95 up ~2.5x for short requests (<=64 tokens). looked like routing put a bunch of short requests onto the long-seq decode path
maya: same cluster? which model / kernel combo?
ben: hosted-canary-1, model=v1.3.0-quant, kernel=fused_attn_optim, route=length-bucketed -> prefill-decoder-long-path
kevin: that's strange — fused_attn_optim should be faster for short seqs. any autotune logs?
ben: pulled an autotune diff, see snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:11Z] autotune: selected_kernel=fused_attn_optim for seq>=512
[2026-03-15T08:12:12Z] routing: bucket=short_seq (<=64) -> path=DECODE_LONG (hysteresis=1.2)
[2026-03-15T08:12:12Z] perf: p50=34ms p95=220ms (baseline p50=13ms p95=90ms)
```
sasha: aha that routing line. looks like hysteresis/threshold math moved some short requests into the long path. maybe a mis-evaluated distribution sample?
maya: or KV cache behavior — if KV cache miss triggers prefill-like work, short decode could end up doing extra copy/deserialize on the long path. any KV logs?
ben: yes, KV miss rate spiked for the same window. small sample: 
```
kv_cache: miss_rate=0.27 -> 0.71 (during spike)
io: extra_copy_bytes_perreq=12KB
```
kevin: 12KB extra copy per request for short payloads is significant. combined with long-path kernels it explains p95 blowup.
maya: quick triage suggestion: 1) force short-path kernel pick for seq <= 128 as a temporary feature flag 2) tighten bucket hysteresis from 1.2 -> 1.05 3) probe KV warmup strategy (prefetch last N keys)
sasha: +1. also add metric to track "route_mismatch" = count(requests where chosen_path != optimal_for_seq) so autotune can see regression
ben: trying the FF now. repro command I'm using: 
```
./tools/bench --model v1.3.0-quant --seq 32 --concurrency 48 --profile=on --route=autotune
```
runtime-bot: deploy 183567-proto to cluster hosted-canary-1 scheduled by ben at 2026-03-15T09:03:00Z :rocket:
kevin: if you can capture a perf profile (pprof) for a few slow requests that will show where time is spent — decode vs kernel vs memcpy vs KV io
ben: uploaded profiles to /mnt/capture/183567/ — pprof shows most time in memcpy + kernel launch overhead, not kernel compute itself
maya: kernel launch overhead + memcpy points to path mismatch and extra cache copies. do we have a fast path which avoids serializing KV when token_count small?
sasha: there is a short-path fastpath but the router bypasses it when estimated sequence length jitter > hysteresis. autotune probably adjusted hysteresis based on noisy length samples from a bad sampling window
kevin: propose change: revert hysteresis to 1.0 in canary and add a conservative cooldown window for autotune adjustments (e.g., do not change thresholds more than once per 30m per model)
ben: testing FF for short-path-for-<=128 and hysteresis=1.0 on canary now. early numbers: p50 -> 12ms p95 -> 92ms (closer to baseline)
maya: good. postmortem action items: - add route_mismatch metric - add autotune cooldown - improve KV warmup heuristic for low-token requests - add unit test that simulates high KV miss spike to ensure routing doesn't flip
sasha: i'll own route_mismatch metric + dashboard (sasha)
kevin: i'll own autotune cooldown change + unit tests (kevin)
ben: i'll follow up on KV warmup tweak and keep canary running for 6 hours (ben)
runtime-bot: deploy 183567-revert-hysteresis completed on hosted-canary-1 at 2026-03-15T09:45:20Z :white_check_mark:
ben: after 2h: route_mismatch down from 18% -> 1.2%, p95 stable near baseline. leaving canary overnight then will roll to staging
maya: nice work. let's also annotate the autotune logs (add reason tags) so we can trace why thresholds shifted next time
ben: noted. closing thread after rollout unless anyone sees further regressions :)
